newsitem.title: USA: Chesapeake Energy sets drilling writedown.
newsitem.headline: Chesapeake Energy sets drilling writedown.

text.p: Chesapeake Energy Corp said Friday it expects to incur a fourth quarter, ending June 30, pretax writedown of about $150-$200 million as a result of disappointing drilling results in Louisiana outside of Masters Creek.

The company said it has refocused its Louisiana Austin Chalk trend drilling into the Masters Creek area and will take the writedown due to the significant leasehold and drilling costs associated with its investments outside this area.
Chesapeake Energy Corp said its Louisiana rig count is expected to remain at eight-to-twelve rather than increasing to the previously planed 15-to-20 rigs.

The company said it estimates 75 to 80 percent of these rigs will work in developing its inventory of some 200 drillsites in Masters Creek. The others will woirk in devloping more limited areas in South Brookeland, St. Landry, Baton Rouge and Livingston.

As a consequence of the refocused Louisiana drilling program, Chesapeake said, it has reduced fiscal 1998 and 1999 capital budgets to $275 to $300 million per year from the previously forcast $400 to $435 million.

The lower spending will lead to reduced production growth in both years, the company said, adding it now projects production of 21.5 to 22 billion cubic feet equivalent for the current quarter and about 80 billion for fiscal 1997.
It said the new estimate for next year is 95 to 100 billion cubic feet and some 115 to 120 billion in fiscal 1999.
Analysts' estimates of cash flow from operations and earnings for fiscal 1998 and 1999 will need to be reduced accordingly, Chesapeake's statement continued.
Company officials were not immediately available to comment on its previous production estimates.

The company also said it has a backlog of more than 1,000 undrilled locations in the five major drilling programs where it is active in Louisiana, Texas, Oklahoma, New Mexico and North Dakota/Montana.
"We also have cash and investments of approximately $250 million that sould fund our anticipated drilling program through at least fiscal 1999.
"Additionally, as evidence of our confidence in the future of our Lousisana drilling activities, a common stock repurchase program is under consideration," the statement concluded.
It said an operations undate and cvonference call will be scheduled in July.
